DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwm.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 47 s. 2023 20 207) Atty. JERIE MARPAPAO RAGSAC Acting Provincial Officer National Commission on Indigenous Peoples Misamis Oriental Provincial Office General Antonio Luna St., Capitol Compound Cagayan de Oro City Dear Atty. Ragsac: This refers to your letter dated March 7, 2023, requesting this Department's legal opinion on the creation of tribal barangays. Specifically, the queries proffered for this Department's opinion are as follows: I. Can the tribal barangay set their manner of election other than that provided under RA 7160? 2. Can the appointed officials (Barangay Secretary and Treasurer) be appointed by the Indigenous Political Structure (IPS) instead of the Punong Barangay and the concurrence of the majority of the Sangguniang Barangay? and 3. Can the removal of an elected tribal barangay official be placed at the discretion of the Indigenous Political Structure (IPS) instead of the processes provided for in the Local Government Code? Per your letter, the foregoing queries stemmed from the request of the Higaonon ICC/lPs of Misamis Oriental regarding the drafting of local guidelines on the creation of tribal barangays in Misamis Oriental. We deem it apt to address the foregoing queries in one discussion as they are essentially interrelated. Pursuant to Republic Act (RA) 8371, othemise known as "The Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997", the constitution of the tribal barangays must be in accordance with the Local Government Code on the creation of tribal barangays. In particular, Section 18 thereof expressly provides: "Section 18. Tribal Barangays. The ICCs/lPs living in contiguous areas or communities where they form the predominant population but which are located in municipalities, provinces or cities where they do not constitute the majority of the population, may form or constitute a separate barangay in accordance with the Local Government Code on the creation of tribal barangays." (Emphasis supplied) Matinq, Mahusay at Maasahan"

Corollarily, Sections 385 and 386 of the Local Government Code of 1991 govern the manner of the creation of barangays, thus: "Section 385. Manner of Creation. - A barangay may be created, divided, merged, abolished, or its boundary substantially altered, by law or by an ordinance of the sangguniang panlalawigan or panlungsod, subject to approval by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite to be conducted by the COMELEC in the local government unit or units directly affected within such period of time as may be determined by the law or ordinance creating said barangay. In the case of the creation of barangays by the sangguniang panlalawigan, the recommendation of the sangguniang bayan concerned shall be necessary. Section 386. Requisites for Creation. - (a) A barangay may be created out of a contiguous territory which has a population of at least two thousand (2,000) inhabitants as certified by the National Statistics Office except in cities and municipalities within Metro Manila and other metropolitan political subdivisions or in highly urbanized cities where such territory shall have a certified population of at least five thousand (5,000) inhabitants: Provided, That the creation thereof shall not reduce the population of the original barangay or barangays to less than the minimum requirement prescribed herein. To enhance the delivery of basic services in the indigenous cultural communities, barangays may be created in such communities by an Act of Congress, notwithstanding the above requirement. (b) The territorial jurisdiction of the new barangay shall be properly identified by metes and bounds or by more or less permanent natural boundaries. The territory need not be contiguous if it comprises two (2) or more islands. (c) The governor or city mayor may prepare a consolidation plan for barangays, based on the criteria prescribed in this Section, within his territorial jurisdiction. The plan shall be submitted to the sangguniang panlalawigan or sangguniang panlungsod concerned for appropriate action. In the case of municipalities within the Metropolitan Manila Area and other metropolitan political subdivisions, the barangay consolidation plan shall be prepared and approved by the sangguniang bayan concerned." (Emphasis supplied) Attention is respectfully directed to the highlighted provision, which allows the relaxation of the requirements for the creation of barangays and sanctions the creation of barangays in indigenous cultural communities by an Act of Congress. Regrettably, to date, there is no provision under the Local Government Code that provides for the creation of tribal barangays, nor is there any act of Congress to effectuate the same. Verily, while Republic Act No. 8371 provides that tribal barangays may be formed or constituted as separate barangays, this provision is not self-executing—it requires supplementary or enabling legislation for its enforcement. Page 2 of 2

Accordingly, this Department submits that in the absence of an enabling law to enforce the creation of tribal barangays pursuant to Section 18 of RA 8371, the Local Government Code remains the prevailing law insofar as the creation of barangays is concerned. Thus, the foregoing queries must be answered in the negative. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, y the A thority of th ecretary: AN ICTOR R.
